Vincent marks one other departure from the Ms. by brackets rather than a footnote ([ἡ] δίεσις, 340.11). Note 1 is a conjecture, not a Ms. report. 'P reads πεποίηνται' is therefore a sound argument from silence, not a reported reading.

Bas. 27.5-6 and H 66r.7-8 read «ἕτερα ἀσύνθετα διαστήματα γίνεται», and so do Par. 23r.2-3 and V 77v.21-78r.1. Vinc. 340.1 has the same. In «Οὕτως οὖν ἔχει περὶ τοὺς λόγους καὶ τὰ … διαστήματα» (340.24-25) the noun depends on περί, so it is not a counter-example.

A. 1.7.17. §959a: 'With the above exception Attic regularly uses the singular verb.'

checks.correction: The musical citations are correct: «ἁρμονίας ῥυθμοῖς κραθείσας» (Pl.Lg.835b) and «τῆς εὖ κεκραμένης ἁρμονίας» (Arist.Pol.1290a26). But «ἐν ταῖς εὖ κεκρ. πολιτείαις» is not the entry's only use with ἐν + dative. LSJ also cites «οἶνον… ἐνὶ κρητῆρι κέρωνται» (Il. 4.260) and «ἐν τῷ ποτηρίῳ ᾧ ἐκέρασε» (Apoc. 18.6). Both are locative too ('in the bowl/cup'), so the finding's conclusion still holds: there is no lexicon example of ἐν + dative meaning 'mixed into'. For the perfect participle, Pol. 1307b30 is indeed the only ἐν example.

checks.correction: The material is under II.4.b, not II.4. The examples of δέδοκται itself are Hdt. 4.68 and S. Ph. 1277. Pl. Lg. 799e has δεδόχθω, and S. Ant. 576 has δεδογμέν' [ἐστί]. The gloss 'visum est' is not in LSJ. The idiom is supported, and II.5 ('be an established opinion', Arist. APo. 76b24) is also relevant.

The examples are accurately reported: Jos. Ap. 1.23, Cleomed. 37.1, John 3:18, and Lucian, Aristides, Justin, Cyril H. §1818 sits on p. 430, and §1945 begins on p. 452, with 'Negation οὐ' on p. 453. But Jannaris presents μή with the indicative after ὅτι/ἐπεί as an intrusion: 'its aggression on the indicative met with a successful resistance… the instances… are not of such number and character as to have influenced the ultimate issue'. So 'how' should call causal ὅτι μηδέ an attested post-classical usage (his note adds: even in Atticistic writers), not 'normal'.

The summary of Smyth is accurate. §2760 deals with a simple negative after a negative, which keeps its force or makes an affirmative; the example is οὐδεὶς οὐκ ἔπασχέ τι. §2761 says a compound negative after a negative confirms it. The application in 'how' is doubtful. οὔ πω (= οὔπω) is ordinarily treated as a compound of οὐ (cf. §2688), so by §2761 it would confirm μηδέ rather than cancel it. These sections do not show that reading 2's negation cancels. What they leave is the mixture of the μή and οὐ series and the redundancy.

checks.source: E. A. Sophocles, Greek Lexicon of the Roman and Byzantine Periods (1914 printing)
checks.correction: The lexicon does have a headword παιάν: «παιάν, ᾶνος, ὁ, = παίων, the foot ⏑⏑⏑–. Aristot. Rhet. 3, 8, 4.6. Dion. H. V, 204, 14, 205, 13». It also has «παίων, ωνος, ὁ, paeon, the foot … Dion. H., Drac., Heph. 3, 8, Ps.-Demetr., Aristid. Q. 38. 39», besides παιανικός, παιανισμός and παιανογράφος. Both headwords are given only for the metrical foot. There is no παιήων and no entry for the song sense, so the lexicon still says nothing about which form Byzantine authors preferred for the song.

summary:
I checked all 30 findings of R4. 21 are confirmed, 8 corrected and 1 is wrong.

The wrong one is place 25 #3. Sophocles' lexicon does have headwords παιάν (= παίων, the metrical foot) and παίων; the finding said it had none.

Corrections:
- Place 21 #0: Vincent's ἐξ φθάρσεως also drops the υ of Ms. ἐξυφθάρσεως; it is not just a word division.
- Place 21 #4: on the same lsj.gr page, the Greek Liddell-Scott entry for φθάρσις cites this very passage (Psellus ap. Vincent p. 340.10), so that attestation is circular. Only Bailly's Ocellus reference is independent, and I could not verify it.
- Place 22 #3: LSJ s.v. κεράννυμι also has ἐν + dative at Il. 4.260 and Apoc. 18.6. Both are locative, so the finding's conclusion still holds.
- Place 23 #3: the material is LSJ δοκέω II.4.b. The examples of δέδοκται itself are Hdt. 4.68 and S. Ph. 1277; Pl. Lg. 799e has δεδόχθω and S. Ant. 576 has δεδογμέν'.
- Place 23 #4: §1818 is on p. 430. Jannaris calls μή with the indicative after causal ὅτι a limited intrusion, so it is attested, not 'normal'.
- Place 23 #5: οὔ πω is ordinarily a compound negative, so by Smyth §2761 it would confirm μηδέ, not cancel it.
- Places 21 #1, 22 #1, 23 #0, 20 #4 and 24 #0 carry only small location or caveat notes.

Files I downloaded for checking are in work-v/r4v_dl.
